vesta.extension.description: Vesta language support (.vx): LSP server, semantic highlighting, diagnostics and compiler views (IR, bytecode, JIT/AOT, diagrams and complexity).
vesta.token.escapeSequence.description: Escape sequence inside a string or character literal.
vesta.token.register.description: Machine register inside an asm block.
vesta.restartServer.title: Restart the language server
vesta.stopServer.title: Stop the language server (frees its binary)
vesta.showServerLog.title: Show the server log
vesta.openStdlib.title: Open a standard library module
vesta.openImport.title: Open the imported module under the cursor
vesta.showPaths.title: Show the paths in use
vesta.showIr.title: View the SSA IR
vesta.showIrDiff.title: View the IR diff (before and after optimising)
vesta.showBytecode.title: View the .vel bytecode
vesta.showJitAsm.title: View the JIT assembly
vesta.showAotAsm.title: View the AOT assembly
vesta.showComplexity.title: View each function's cost and contracts
vesta.showModes.title: View the report of the three execution modes
vesta.showAotCompat.title: View AOT compatibility
vesta.showMacroExpand.title: View the macro expansion
vesta.showComptimeValues.title: View the comptime values
vesta.showAsa.title: View everything the compiler knows about the module
vesta.selectTarget.title: Choose what the inspected code is compiled for
vesta.runCell.title: Run the cell
vesta.runSelection.title: Run the selection
vesta.selectRunOptions.title: Choose how it runs (mode, optimisation, debugging)
vesta.showDiagram.title: View a diagram of the module
vesta.showMachineView.title: View the source / IR / assembly correlation
vesta.compile.title: Compile the active file
vesta.run.title: Compile and run the active file
vesta.showAsmBlock.title: View the assembly block with its flow
vesta.server.path.description: Path to the `vesta_lsp` executable. Empty = automatic search: the `VESTA_LSP` environment variable, `PATH`, the install roots (`%ProgramFiles%\VestaVM\bin`, `VESTA_HOME`, `/usr/local/vesta`, ...) and the repository build directories (`cmake-build-release/`, `build/`).
vesta.server.arguments.description: Extra arguments for the language server.
vesta.server.enable.description: Start the language server when a .vx file is opened. With it off only grammar highlighting remains.
vesta.trace.server.description: Trace level of the protocol between the editor and the language server.
vesta.stdlibPath.description: Path of the `stdlib/vx` directory holding the standard library written in Vesta. Empty = automatic search: the `VX_STDLIB_DIR` environment variable, the language server's own folder (`<install>/stdlib/vx`) and the repository tree. This is the library that go-to-definition on a `std.*` symbol jumps into.
vesta.vmPath.description: Path to the virtual machine executable (`vesta` once installed, `vm` in the build tree). Empty = the same automatic search as the language server.
vesta.run.mode.description: How the code launched from the editor runs (cells and selection).
vesta.run.mode.vm: Interpreter: the virtual machine runs the bytecode without compiling to native
vesta.run.mode.jit: JIT: the virtual machine compiles to native whatever gets hot
vesta.run.mode.aot: Native: it is compiled to an executable and launched
vesta.run.opt.description: Optimisation level the code being run is compiled with.
vesta.run.debug.description: Compile the code being run with debug information.
vesta.run.timeout.description: Longest a run may take, in milliseconds, before it is cut off. An infinite loop is an ordinary accident while writing.
vesta.reuseTerminal.description: Reuse the same terminal when running programs one after another.
vesta.opt.o0: O0: unoptimised, the code just as it was lowered
vesta.opt.o2: O2: the level things are normally compiled at
vesta.inlayHints.parameterNames.descript: Show each parameter's name in front of its argument at call sites.
vesta.inlayHints.compilerFacts.descripti: Show at the end of each line what the compiler deduces from it: the bounds a value moves between, whether it is constant, what alignment it ends up with, where it points.
vesta.inlayHints.compilerFactsUnknown.de: Also show where the compiler **looked and came up with nothing**, and why. Useful to audit what is known and what is not; on every line it crowds out what IS known, which is why it ships off.
vesta.inspect.os.description: Operating system the code is compiled for: it decides the views (IR, bytecode, assembly and diagrams) and also the errors and the hover, because those come out of compiling. Left empty it analyses for the host, and a module written for another system shows up full of true errors that do not matter there.
vesta.inspect.arch.description: Architecture the code is compiled for: it decides the compiler views and also the errors and the hover. Empty = the host's.
vesta.inspect.opt.description: Optimisation level the code shown in the views is compiled with. Looking at the same code at two levels is how you see what the optimiser did.
vesta.inspect.opt.default: The level the ordinary analysis compiles at
vesta.inspect.floatIsa.description: Floating-point instruction set of the code being shown. Empty = the default one.
vesta.inspect.cpu.description: Specific microarchitecture (`znver3`, `skylake`, ...) the shown code is generated for. Empty = whatever follows from the instruction set. The **Vesta: choose what the inspected code is compiled for** command offers the ones the compiler has timings for.
vesta.aot.tier.description: Runtime tier the AOT views assume (compatibility and the report of the modes).
vesta.diagram.format.description: Format the diagrams are requested from the server in.
vesta.diagram.format.html: Self-contained interactive page, rendered inside the editor
vesta.diagram.cost.description: Annotate the diagram's function nodes with their Big-O cost.
vesta.flowArrows.description: Draws the arrows of the jumps inside asm blocks over the code itself. The compiler computes them -- it already builds each block's flow graph -- and the file is left untouched.
